title: Original pad to Bluetooth keyboard, pad-ble v1
intro: One original NES controller into an ESP32, which presents it to a phone or a laptop as a plain Bluetooth keyboard. It is the bench bridge's own pad poll with a radio behind it instead of a shift register, and it stands alone: no Pi, no UNO, no console.

THIS IS A DRAWING, NOT A BUILD, AND THE PART HAS CHANGED UNDER IT. The ESP32-C6 of sheets 2 to 4 never accepted a flash. On 2026-09-24 a Waveshare ESP32-P4-Module-DEV-KIT flashed first try and put a BLE advertisement on the air that an independent radio heard, so sheets 5 to 10 are that board and are the ones to build from. The C6 sheets stay because a published drawing is a record. Nothing has been wired to either.

IT RESTS ON ONE THING OPEN SINCE 2026-09-07: that an original pad's 4021 follows its buttons at 3.3 V. The datasheet says it should; this bench has not seen it. The P4's header was read from Waveshare's own schematic, not off the board, and the lead colours are looked up from the cable as it was rung out: rev E carried three of five wrong because they were typed from memory.
revisions: drawn as the buildable subset of the pad adapter: no cell, no charger, no switch
S3 pin numbers removed; GPIO4, GPIO5 and GPIO15 are strapping pins on the C6
one pullup per pad: R1 and R2 had both been drawn on pad 1's data line
devkit headers read off the part, breadboard sheet drawn from them
the second pad removed: a keyboard report has six key slots, and it was never sent
the sheet's own summary stopped saying a second pad is polled; it is not
the devkit's two header rows were drawn swapped; every address moves from row J to row A
the board built is the Waveshare ESP32-P4-Module-DEV-KIT; its header read from the vendor schematic and added as a sheet
the P4 gets its own three drawings; three of the five lead colours in rev E were typed, not read, and are corrected
